gloss: Squeezing toothpaste; to do something slowly and reluctantly.
teaser: Ever wondered how a simple tube of toothpaste can teach us about patience and effort?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wondered how a simple tube of toothpaste can teach us about patience and effort? [break 1s] The phrase is: 挤牙膏, jǐ yágāo. [break 0.5s] 挤 (jǐ) means "to squeeze" [break 0.5s] 牙 (yá) means "tooth" [break 0.5s] 膏 (gāo) means "paste" [break 1s] So, the full idiom again is: 挤牙膏; literally, it means "squeezing toothpaste," and figuratively, it refers to doing something slowly and reluctantly. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] The idiom originates from the common practice of squeezing toothpaste from a tube. People often try to get the last bit out, doing it little by little. This reflects how in life, some tasks can feel like you're trying to extract every last bit of effort, often requiring patience and persistence. [break 1.5s] Example 1: 他做这个项目像挤牙膏一样，进展缓慢。 [break 1s] He is making progress on this project like squeezing toothpaste, slowly. [break 1s] Example 2: 她对这个问题的回答就像挤牙膏，迟迟不肯说出。 [break 1s] Her response to the question was like squeezing toothpaste, reluctant to come out. [break 1s] Example 3: 我们的预算被挤牙膏一样，越来越紧。 [break 1s] Our budget feels like it's being squeezed like toothpaste, getting tighter and tighter. [break 1s] So, remember the idiom: 挤牙膏, which means to do something slowly and reluctantly. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
